collection: NERDC JSS 1 Physical and Health Education soccer and field events
note: Original classroom practice. Field-event items assess observation and safety reasoning. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Control a rolling pass and return it accurately in a supervised drill.
questions.prompt: With a partner and a soft football, use the marked practice lane. Receive a gentle rolling pass and bring the ball under control. Then pass it back along the ground through the cone gate. Take two turns each while the teacher observes.
questions.answer: A pupil cushions the incoming ball so it remains within playing distance, then sends a controlled rolling pass through the gate.
questions.explanation: A controlled first touch makes the next action easier. A ground pass through a gate gives a visible test of direction.

markingGuide.description: Keeps the first touch within playing distance.
Sends the return pass along the ground.
Directs at least one return pass through the gate.
Takes turns and stays in the marked lane.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Select a ball-control adjustment for a tight turn.
questions.prompt: During a cone drill, the ball repeatedly rolls beyond Chidi’s reach just before a turn. Which adjustment is most likely to help him change direction while keeping the ball close?
questions.answer: Slow slightly and use shorter touches before the turn.
questions.explanation: Shorter touches reduce the distance the ball travels away from the player and allow time to change direction.
options: Kick the ball farther ahead before turning.
Increase speed while keeping the same long touches.
Slow slightly and use shorter touches before the turn.
Run around the cone first and leave the ball behind.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Apply the whole-ball crossing and last-touch criteria to a throw-in decision.
questions.prompt: In a match using IFAB Law 15, the ball first rolls with part of it still over the touchline. It then passes completely beyond the line after a Blue player’s touch. What should the match official decide at each point?
questions.answer: Play continues at the first point because the whole ball has not crossed. At the second point, award a throw-in to the other team because Blue touched it last.
questions.explanation: The restart follows complete crossing of the touchline. The opposing team of the last player to touch it takes the throw-in.

markingGuide.description: Keeps play going while part of the ball remains over the line.
Identifies a throw-in after full crossing.
Awards it to the team opposing Blue.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Explain why access to a throwing sector is controlled during school field events.
questions.prompt: A teacher is supervising a field-event demonstration. One pupil wants to collect an implement from the landing area while the next demonstrator is getting ready. Describe what the pupil should do and explain why.
questions.answer: Stay outside the landing area and wait for the teacher to stop activity and give permission to collect it.
questions.explanation: Keeping people out of the landing area while a throw could occur reduces the chance of someone being struck.

markingGuide.description: Waits for an explicit teacher signal after activity is stopped.
Explains the risk of an implement striking someone.

questions.subject: Physical and Health Education
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish the basic delivery actions shown in shot put and discus demonstrations.
questions.prompt: Two paused demonstration clips show different implements. In clip P an athlete begins with a round shot close to the neck and pushes it away with one hand. In clip Q an athlete carries a disc away from the body and releases it after a sweeping arm action. Identify each event and give one observable clue for each.
questions.answer: P is shot put, shown by the shot starting close to the neck and being pushed. Q is discus, shown by the disc and the sweeping delivery.
questions.explanation: The implement and the observed delivery distinguish the events. This observation task assesses recognition of techniques.

markingGuide.description: Gives an observed clue for P.
Gives an observed clue for Q.
